pages.title: Big Five personality: understand the five OCEAN dimensions
pages.summary: A bounded guide to reading five continuous trait dimensions as hypotheses for observation rather than fixed identity labels.

sections.heading: What is the Big Five?
sections.body: The Big Five organizes personality-trait descriptions into openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism. The five dimensions describe degrees of tendency, not a fixed type or a complete account of a person.

sections.heading: OCEAN in one view
sections.body: The five headings cover engagement with novelty, organization and follow-through, social energy, cooperation, and sensitivity to distress. They are broad observation lenses rather than rankings of character or ability.

sections.heading: Think in ranges
sections.body: A dimensional score sits on a continuum. High, middle, and low positions can all be adaptive in some settings, and the same person may express a tendency differently when the goal, role, or pressure changes.

sections.heading: Read a pattern, then test it
sections.body: Compare all five dimensions, find repeated behavior across at least two contexts, and inspect facets or counterexamples before accepting a description. A mismatch is useful evidence and should not be edited away.

sections.heading: Use facets for a narrower question
sections.body: A domain gives the broad map; facets provide more specific navigation. Follow the facet hub only when a domain summary is too coarse, and keep the named measurement taxonomy explicit rather than merging different systems.

sections.heading: Appropriate uses
sections.body: Use the model to organize reflection about planning, learning, communication, novelty, and pressure. Do not use it as a clinical diagnosis, hiring cutoff, admission rule, or deterministic prediction of performance or relationships.

sections.heading: Common reading errors
sections.body: High is not automatically better, low is not automatically deficient, and one score is not a permanent verdict. Group-level change research cannot predict an individual's trajectory or guarantee an intervention result.

sections.heading: Context changes expression
sections.body: Jordan uses a checklist for a regulated release but explores freely during an early design workshop. The contrasting behaviors show why task stakes and purpose must be considered before summarizing a broad tendency.

sections.heading: Look for disconfirming evidence
sections.body: Someone who stays quiet in a large meeting may facilitate an energetic small-group review. Status, preparation, language, and psychological safety are alternatives to a broad conclusion about social energy.

sections.heading: Pair benefit with cost
sections.body: Detailed planning can prevent missed handoffs but delay a reversible choice; rapid exploration can generate options but make completion harder. Judge the behavior against the goal, time, and error cost.

sections.heading: Seven-day observation
sections.body: Record situation, behavior, consequence, and one alternative explanation for a single reported tendency. Include two settings and one counterexample, then keep, narrow, or reject the hypothesis.

sections.heading: Method boundary
sections.body: The sources support broad trait structure, hierarchical description, and group-level change findings. They do not independently validate FermatMind scores, establish a universal facet taxonomy, diagnose an individual, or guarantee outcomes.

sections.heading: Sources and limitations
sections.body: The page maps five-dimension claims to Goldberg and the BFI-2, hierarchy claims to the BFI-2, and change claims to a life-course meta-analysis. Each citation retains its limitation.

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.body: Choose a domain guide for a broad question, the facet hub for a narrower pattern, or the test overview for product boundaries. All links remain within the English public information architecture.

visible_sources.limitation: Supports broad factor structure, not FermatMind score validity or a universal facet taxonomy.
Describes one 15-facet model; taxonomies are not automatically interchangeable.
Group-level change does not predict or guarantee individual change.

pages.title: 大五人格 OCEAN 指南：把五维结果变成可检验的观察
pages.summary: 从五个连续维度整理行为线索，用场景和反例核对结果，不把分数写成固定身份。

sections.heading: 大五人格是什么
sections.body: 大五人格把特质描述整理为开放性、尽责性、外向性、宜人性和神经质五个宽泛维度。它描述倾向的程度，不把人归入固定类型，也不能代替对经历和情境的理解。

sections.heading: OCEAN 在观察什么
sections.body: 五个入口分别关注新想法与体验、安排与执行、社交活力、合作与体谅、压力和负面情绪敏感度。名称用于组织观察，不表示道德或能力等级。

sections.heading: 用程度而不是类别来读
sections.body: 连续维度允许高、中、低和混合倾向同时成为有用信息。同一个人在不同任务、角色和压力下也会表现不同，因此分数应与具体行为一起解释。

sections.heading: 先看组合，再找证据
sections.body: 先比较五维组合，再从两个以上情境寻找重复模式，最后用侧面与反例核对。文字若与经验不符，应保留不一致，而不是为了证明报告正确去拼接故事。

sections.heading: 需要更具体时再进入侧面
sections.body: 维度提供地图，侧面帮助缩小问题。只有总体描述过粗时才进入侧面总览，并明确使用的测量体系，避免把不同模型中的标签和数量混为一谈。

sections.heading: 适合与不适合的用途
sections.body: 可以用它复盘学习、计划、沟通、变化和压力下的行为；不能把它当作临床诊断、招聘门槛、录取规则或对工作与关系结果的决定性预测。

sections.heading: 三个误区
sections.body: 高分不自动更好，低分不自动是缺陷，当前结果也不是终身判决。群体层面的变化研究无法预测某个人的轨迹，更不保证一次练习会改变分数。

sections.heading: 场景会改变行为表达
sections.body: 周宁在财务交付前逐项核对，却在概念讨论中允许议题自由展开。两次行为分别服务于降低风险和寻找可能，不能只取其中一次概括整个人。

sections.heading: 主动寻找反例
sections.body: 在大会上沉默的人，可能在熟悉的小组里清楚地主持讨论。角色、准备、语言和安全感都可能解释差异，不能把一次沉默直接等同于宽泛特质。

sections.heading: 同时写出收益和成本
sections.body: 细致计划能减少遗漏，也可能拖慢可逆决定；快速探索能增加方案，也可能妨碍收尾。判断应回到目标、时间、可逆性和出错成本。

sections.heading: 七天观察
sections.body: 选择一个倾向，记录情境、行为、后果和另一个解释；覆盖两个不同场合并寻找一个反例。七天后再决定保留、缩小还是放弃这个假设。

sections.heading: 方法边界
sections.body: 来源支持宽泛结构、层级描述和群体变化，不独立验证费马测试分数，也不证明存在通用侧面体系。内容用于反思，不提供诊断、录用结论或结果保证。

sections.heading: 可见证据
sections.body: 五维结构对应 Goldberg 和 BFI-2 研究，层级说明限定在已声明模型，变化表述限定在生命历程元分析的群体层面。每条来源保留限制。

sections.heading: 下一步导航
sections.body: 宽泛问题进入维度页，更细问题进入侧面总览，产品边界进入测试说明。链接保持中文语境，从总览逐步收窄问题。
